Attendees can explore highlights from industry-leading brake assemblies, designed to deliver unmatched stopping power and durability in off-highway environments. The display will also feature both the EPD and N680 advanced friction technologies, built to optimize performance and reliability in high-torque applications. Together, these products represent a century of engineering excellence and a future-focused commitment to solving the toughest challenges in agricultural mobility.
paras.zh: 分享一系列强大的制动系统解决方案，专为满足现代农业设备的需求而设计。与会者可以探索行业领先的制动组件的亮点，这些组件旨在在非公路环境中提供无与伦比的制动力和耐用性。该显示器还将采用 EPD 和 N680 先进摩擦技术，旨在优化高扭矩应用中的性能和可靠性。这些产品共同代表了一个世纪以来的卓越工程技术和着眼于未来解决农业移动领域最严峻挑战的承诺。

paras.en: Showcasing the leading on-board computing platform for machine intelligence and HMI solutions. New products, designed specifically to meet the needs of agricultural machinery, include 10- and 12-inch smart terminals, central vehicle computing with monitors, and 5- and 7-inch displays featuring programmable soft keys for tactile control. The CCpilot V1090 and V1290 are the first displays with an integrated network switch that makes it easier to incorporate elements like camera systems, sensors and precision systems, into one display computer. The vehicle computer and monitors (CrossCore A100 with monitors from 10 to 12 inches) highlight the new centralized computing architecture. This approach provides a flexible, scalable platform for vehicle intelligence. It includes innovative component life cycle management and increased support for functional safety.
paras.zh: 展示用于机器智能和 HMI 解决方案的领先机载计算平台。专为满足农业机械需求而设计的新产品包括10英寸和12英寸智能终端、带显示器的中央车辆计算以及具有用于触觉控制的可编程软键的5英寸和7英寸显示器。 CCpilot V1090 和 V1290 是首款具有集成网络交换机的显示器，可以更轻松地将摄像头系统、传感器和精密系统等元素整合到一台显示计算机中。车载电脑和显示器（CrossCore A100，显示器尺寸从10英寸到12英寸）突出了新的集中式计算架构。这种方法为车辆智能提供了一个灵活、可扩展的平台。它包括创新的组件生命周期管理和增加对功能安全的支持。

paras.en: Highlighting how Elliott’s flexible planting products deliver precision performance, highly operational reliability and mechanical advantages without the need for additional power sources. The flexible drive and control shaft products bring enhanced performance to original equipment machinery, providing simple and dependable aftermarket upgrades for an ongoing return on your investment. Five different flexible drive shaft agricultural systems are available, and the assemblies fit most planters on the market today.
paras.zh: 重点介绍 Elliott 的灵活种植产品如何在无需额外电源的情况下提供精确的性能、高度的运行可靠性和机械优势。灵活的驱动和控制轴产品为原始设备机械带来了增强的性能，提供简单可靠的售后升级，为您带来持续的投资回报。有五种不同的柔性驱动轴农业系统可供选择，这些组件适合当今市场上的大多数播种机。

paras.en: Featuring the latest innovations in thermal management solutions, including intake throttle valves, hot- and cold-side exhaust gas recirculation valves, and exhaust back-pressure valves for diesel, gas and hydrogen internal combustion engines.
paras.zh: 采用热管理解决方案的最新创新，包括柴油、燃气和氢气内燃机的进气节流阀、热侧和冷侧废气再循环阀以及排气背压阀。

paras.en: Presenting the latest solutions to help operators sense, see and know more. Show attendees will find a broad portfolio of products, including displays, clusters and sensors for vehicle and equipment monitoring in demanding applications. The displays are built on a microcontroller architecture which offers lean performance with inherent support for key features including fast boot (typically around a second for instant access to machine data). Visitors to Agritechnica can get a hands-on look at the display range, from 1.3 to 4.3 inches, with demos to show general I/O, CAN channel support and application examples. The displays can share multiple screens of information, with intuitive navigation, including diagnostic codes and machine status. The platform offers devices with robust and compact housings suitable to withstand the toughest environments and designed to easily fit 52 or 86 mm SAE case sizes to make installation simple for new and existing cabins.
paras.zh: 呈现最新的解决方案，帮助操作员感知、看到和了解更多。展会与会者将发现广泛的产品组合，包括用于在要求苛刻的应用中监控车辆和设备的显示器、仪表组和传感器。这些显示器基于微控制器架构构建，可提供精益性能以及对快速启动（通常大约一秒即可即时访问机器数据）等关键功能的固有支持。 Agritechnica 的参观者可以亲身体验从 1.3 英寸到 4.3 英寸的显示屏范围，并通过演示展示通用 I/O、CAN 通道支持和应用示例。这些显示器可以共享多个信息屏幕，并具有直观的导航功能，包括诊断代码和机器状态。该平台提供的设备具有坚固而紧凑的外壳，适合承受最恶劣的环境，并可轻松安装 52 或 86 毫米 SAE 外壳尺寸，使新的和现有的驾驶室的安装变得简单。

paras.en: Showcasing the Power-Packer portfolio of manual and electric pumps and cylinders for hydraulic cab tilt and hood-lift applications, as well as the latest electro-hydraulic actuator. All products are designed with a focus on efficiency and perfectly suited for power-on-demand functions in mobile applications. Hydraulic solutions offer precise motion control and ensure reliable performance in the most demanding environments.
paras.zh: 展示用于液压驾驶室倾斜和发动机罩升降应用的手动和电动泵和油缸的 Power-Packer 产品组合，以及最新的电动液压执行器。所有产品的设计都注重效率，非常适合移动应用中的按需供电功能。液压解决方案提供精确的运动控制，并确保在最苛刻的环境中提供可靠的性能。

paras.en: Learn about Weasler’s range of products, from drive shafts and torque limiters to dampers and other components, all designed using the best technology to solve our customers’ power transmission problems. Products are engineered for reliability and precision, ensuring the seamless operation and longevity of agricultural equipment.
paras.zh: 了解 Weasler 的产品系列，从传动轴和扭矩限制器到阻尼器和其他组件，所有产品均采用最佳技术设计，旨在解决客户的动力传输问题。产品的设计注重可靠性和精度，确保农业设备的无缝运行和使用寿命。

articles.title: Introducing the 2026 Class of BodyShop Business Women in Collision
articles.author: Jason Stahl

paras.en: Presenting the 2026 Class of BodyShop Business Women in Collision, highlighting an exceptional group of female collision repair professionals who are making meaningful contributions in the industry. This year’s class represents an impressive range of organizations, from collision facilities to manufacturers and suppliers.
paras.zh: 介绍 2026 届 BodyShop 碰撞行业女性商界人士，重点关注一群杰出的女性碰撞修复专业人士，她们在行业中做出了有意义的贡献。今年的课程代表了一系列令人印象深刻的组织，从碰撞设施到制造商和供应商。

paras.en: The collision repair industry has traditionally been male-dominated, but women are increasingly making their mark across virtually every corner of the business. From repairing vehicles on the shop floor and managing high-performing collision centers to developing business strategies, supporting repairers and building companies of their own, women are helping shape where the industry goes next. Their career paths are as varied as the roles they hold, demonstrating there is no single route to building a successful career in collision repair.
paras.zh: 碰撞修复行业传统上由男性主导，但女性越来越多地在该行业的几乎每个角落留下自己的印记。从车间维修车辆和管理高性能碰撞中心到制定业务战略、支持维修商和建立自己的公司，女性正在帮助塑造该行业的下一步发展方向。他们的职业道路与他们所担任的角色一样多种多样，这表明在碰撞修复领域建立成功的职业生涯并没有单一的途径。

paras.en: That diversity is evident in the 2026 Class of BodyShop Business Women in Collision. Some of this year’s honorees grew up around body shops or automotive businesses, while others arrived in collision almost by accident after beginning careers in fields such as accounting, healthcare and education. Their accomplishments include competing in SkillsUSA, growing family businesses, developing future industry talent, leading large collision operations, advocating for independent repairers and helping shop owners strengthen or transition their businesses. Despite those different backgrounds, common themes emerge: taking chances, embracing uncomfortable challenges, continually learning, and recognizing the value of strong mentors and relationships.
paras.zh: 这种多样性在 2026 年 BodyShop 碰撞中的商业女性班级中表现得很明显。今年的一些获奖者是在车身修理厂或汽车企业周围长大的，而另一些人则是在会计、医疗保健和教育等领域开始职业生涯后几乎偶然遇到了碰撞。他们的成就包括参加 SkillsUSA 竞赛、发展家族企业、培养未来的行业人才、领导大型碰撞事故处理、倡导独立维修商以及帮助店主加强或转型其业务。尽管背景不同，但出现了共同的主题：抓住机会，接受令人不舒服的挑战，不断学习，并认识到强有力的导师和关系的价值。

paras.en: Perhaps most importantly, these women aren’t simply building impressive careers for themselves. They’re developing employees, mentoring the next generation, strengthening businesses and demonstrating the breadth of opportunities available to women entering the industry today. Their advice to those following them is equally powerful: ask questions, take risks, don’t fear failure and don’t wait until you feel completely ready to step forward.
paras.zh: 也许最重要的是，这些女性不仅仅为自己打造令人印象深刻的职业生涯。她们正在培养员工、指导下一代、加强业务，并向当今进入该行业的女性展示广泛的机会。他们对追随者的建议同样有力：提出问题，承担风险，不要害怕失败，不要等到你觉得完全准备好才继续前进。

paras.en: Stephanie Steelman – Body Technician, DCR Systems
paras.zh: Stephanie Steelman – DCR Systems 车身技术员

paras.en: How did your collision career begin? I started learning the basics of collision repair in high school. I was able to compete in the SkillsUSA collision repair competition at the national level and was awarded 4th place. After high school, I had the opportunity to start working as my father’s apprentice.
paras.zh: 您的碰撞生涯是如何开始的？我在高中时开始学习碰撞修复的基础知识。我参加了国家级 SkillsUSA 碰撞修复比赛并获得了第四名。高中毕业后，我有机会开始作为父亲的学徒工作。

paras.en: What is the proudest accomplishment of your career? Getting my first job at DCR Systems after working for my dad. It felt good, having built the confidence in myself and the skills I had developed to go off on my own. I couldn’t be more proud of what I continue to build for myself with DCR Systems. The team at DCR has mentored me, provided me with many training opportunities and helped me grow in my skills.
paras.zh: 您职业生涯中最值得骄傲的成就是什么？为我父亲工作后，我在 DCR Systems 找到了第一份工作。感觉很好，我对自己建立了信心，并培养了独立发展的技能。我对自己通过 DCR Systems 继续为自己打造的东西感到非常自豪。 DCR 的团队为我提供了指导，为我提供了许多培训机会，并帮助我提高了技能。

paras.en: What would you tell your younger collision self? It’s okay to fail. Repairing cars isn’t easy, and it takes a lot of trial-and-error to improve yourself. Take the feeling of being stumped and use it as encouragement to network, seek new ideas and try different techniques.
paras.zh: 你会对年轻时发生碰撞的自己说什么？失败也没关系。修车并不容易，需要大量的尝试和错误来提高自己。把被难住的感觉当作一种鼓励，去建立人际网络、寻求新的想法并尝试不同的技术。

paras.en: Leila Hobart – Associate Strategy & Portfolio Manager, OEC
paras.zh: Leila Hobart – OEC 战略与投资组合副经理

paras.en: How did your collision career begin? Four years ago, I joined OEC’s Repair Technologies team alongside some of the best mentors in the industry. I didn’t come from automotive — my background is in healthcare and education — but the mission hooked me: helping repairers deliver safe, proper repairs that protect vehicle owners.
paras.zh: 您的碰撞生涯是如何开始的？四年前，我与业内一些最优秀的导师一起加入了 OEC 的维修技术团队。我不是来自汽车行业——我的背景是医疗保健和教育——但我的使命吸引了我：帮助维修人员提供安全、适当的维修，保护车主。

paras.en: What is the proudest accomplishment of your career? There are several that come to mind, including building OEM partnerships and leading WIN’s virtual conference, but the one closest to my heart is building OEC’s repair education program and helping schools put tools and training in the hands of the next generation of talent in our industry.
paras.zh: 您职业生涯中最值得骄傲的成就是什么？我想到的有几个，包括建立 OEM 合作伙伴关系和领导 WIN 的虚拟会议，但最让我感兴趣的是建立 OEC 的维修教育计划，以及帮助学校为我们行业的下一代人才提供工具和培训。

paras.en: What would you tell your younger collision self? Take chances! It’s okay to end up somewhere different than your post-college plan. I went from an audiologist, to managing college programs, to shaping strategy in collision. Though I’ve worn different hats, I’ve found a throughline I’m passionate about — working with great people and making a true difference.
paras.zh: 你会对年轻时发生碰撞的自己说什么？抓住机会！最终去往与大学毕业后计划不同的地方是可以的。我从一名听力学家，到管理大学项目，再到制定冲突策略。尽管我担任过不同的职务，但我找到了一条我热衷的主线——与优秀的人一起工作，做出真正的改变。

paras.en: April Lausch – Collision Center Manager, Faulkner Collision Center
paras.zh: April Lausch – 福克纳碰撞中心碰撞中心经理

paras.en: How did your collision career begin? After college, I began my career with a business background and accepted an office manager position at a collision center. I quickly developed a passion for the industry, learning every aspect of the repair process. That experience inspired me to grow professionally and build a long-term career in collision repair.
paras.zh: 您的碰撞生涯是如何开始的？大学毕业后，我以商业背景开始了我的职业生涯，并接受了碰撞中心的办公室经理职位。我很快就对这个行业产生了热情，学习了维修过程的各个方面。这段经历激励我在专业上不断成长，并在碰撞修复领域建立了长期的职业生涯。

paras.en: What is the proudest accomplishment of your career? Helping build a strong team and creating opportunities for others to grow. Seeing employees develop their skills, advance their careers and deliver exceptional repairs while providing outstanding customer service has been the most rewarding part of my career.
paras.zh: 您职业生涯中最值得骄傲的成就是什么？帮助建立一支强大的团队并为他人创造成长机会。看到员工发展技能、推进职业发展、提供出色的维修服务，同时提供出色的客户服务，这是我职业生涯中最有价值的部分。

paras.en: What would you tell your younger collision self? Believe in yourself, stay curious and never stop learning. Don’t be afraid to ask questions or take on new challenges. Every experience, even the difficult ones, will help you grow into a stronger leader and a better advocate for your team and the collision repair industry.
paras.zh: 你会对年轻时发生碰撞的自己说什么？相信自己，保持好奇心，永不停止学习。不要害怕提出问题或接受新的挑战。每一次经历，即使是困难的经历，都将帮助您成长为更强大的领导者以及您的团队和碰撞修复行业的更好的倡导者。

paras.en: Wendy Patrick – Vice President of Store Operations, Gerber Collision & Glass
paras.zh: Wendy Patrick – Gerber Collision & Glass 商店运营副总裁

paras.en: How did your collision career begin? I started in the industry at 17, working in an independent body shop. I never expected it to become my career, but I quickly realized I loved the work, the people and the constant opportunity to learn. That experience sparked a passion that has stayed with me ever since.
paras.zh: 您的碰撞生涯是如何开始的？我 17 岁开始进入这个行业，在一家独立的车身修理厂工作。我从未想过它会成为我的职业，但我很快意识到我喜欢这份工作、这里的人以及不断的学习机会。那次经历激发了我的热情，从那时起，这种热情就一直伴随着我。

paras.en: What is the proudest accomplishment of your career? I’m proud of the opportunities I’ve had throughout my career, but what means the most to me is helping others grow. Watching people gain confidence, step into leadership roles and succeed in ways they may not have imagined has been the most rewarding part of my journey.
paras.zh: 您职业生涯中最值得骄傲的成就是什么？我为自己在整个职业生涯中获得的机会感到自豪，但对我来说最重要的是帮助他人成长。看着人们获得信心、步入领导岗位并以他们意想不到的方式取得成功，这是我这段旅程中最有价值的部分。

paras.en: What would you tell your younger collision self? Be curious, stay open to learning and don’t be afraid to ask questions. Trust that every challenge will teach you something valuable. Build strong relationships, lead with integrity and remember that the way you treat people will define your career more than any title ever will.
paras.zh: 你会对年轻时发生碰撞的自己说什么？保持好奇心，保持开放的学习态度，不要害怕提问。相信每一次挑战都会教会你一些有价值的东西。建立牢固的关系，以诚信领导，并记住，你待人的方式比任何头衔都更能定义你的职业生涯。

paras.en: Syndey Feehan – General Manager, Fix Auto Maple Grove
paras.zh: Syndey Feehan – Fix Auto Maple Grove 总经理

paras.en: How did your collision career begin? I graduated high school in 2020 and was working towards an internship with a State Farm agent. The testing facilities closed due to COVID, and I had to figure out what I wanted to do — wait or figure something else out. My dad offered me a CSR position at one of our shops, and I found my groove. Six years later on the admin side and I love what I do now more than ever!
paras.zh: 您的碰撞生涯是如何开始的？我于 2020 年高中毕业，正在努力在 State Farm 代理商处实习。由于新冠疫情，测试设施关闭了，我必须弄清楚我想做什么——等待或想出其他办法。我父亲在我们的一家商店为我提供了一个企业社会责任职位，我找到了自己的最佳状态。六年后，在管理方面，我比以往任何时候都更喜欢我现在所做的事情！

paras.en: What is the proudest accomplishment of your career? I’m most proud of the family legacy that I get to help carry on. My brothers and I are the third generation, and the family dynamic is really what I believe sets us apart from our competitors. To work alongside my dad, brothers and husband every day is such a gift. To be able to achieve metrics like the no. 1 GEICO ARX store in the country and having all three of our stores scoring a 99-100 RPM score for State Farm is a testament to our dedication to our work and the grit we have in all that we do.
paras.zh: 您职业生涯中最值得骄傲的成就是什么？我最自豪的是我能帮助延续家族遗产。我和我的兄弟是第三代，我相信家庭活力确实是我们与竞争对手区别开来的原因。每天与我的父亲、兄弟和丈夫一起工作真是一份礼物。能够达到像没有这样的指标。 GEICO ARX 商店在全国排名第一，State Farm 的所有三家商店均获得 99-100 RPM 的评分，这证明了我们对工作的奉献精神以及我们所做的一切的勇气。

paras.en: What would you tell your younger collision self? Be confident in your abilities. Learn all that you can. Watch your own bobber. Always ask questions. It’s okay to be uncomfortable — growth can be scary. Have a thankful heart. You don’t have to do this; you get to do this!
paras.zh: 你会对年轻时发生碰撞的自己说什么？对自己的能力充满信心。尽你所能去学习。小心你自己的浮标。总是问问题。感到不舒服没关系——成长可能会令人恐惧。要有一颗感恩的心。你不必这样做；你必须这样做！

paras.en: Rachel James – Founder, Torque Financial
paras.zh: Rachel James – Torque Financial 创始人

paras.en: How did your collision career begin? My path started in automotive and aviation as a technician before I discovered collision repair at a Chevy/Hyundai dealership. It was a fluke thing really, some employees left and there was a gap on the body shop side and the owner asked if I could go over to collision and help. I quickly fell in love with the creativity, problem-solving and craftsmanship behind collision repair — and I’ve been passionate about the industry ever since.
paras.zh: 您的碰撞生涯是如何开始的？在我在雪佛兰/现代经销店发现碰撞修复之前，我的职业生涯始于汽车和航空技术员。这确实是一件侥幸的事情，一些员工离开了，车身修理厂一侧有一个缺口，车主问我是否可以过去碰撞并提供帮助。我很快就爱上了碰撞修复背后的创造力、解决问题的能力和工艺——从那时起我就对这个行业充满了热情。

paras.en: What is the proudest accomplishment of your career? I’ve been blessed with some great moments, but nothing ever compares to helping blue-collar professionals build stronger businesses, overcome debt or save money for their future.
paras.zh: 您职业生涯中最值得骄傲的成就是什么？我有幸经历过一些伟大的时刻，但没有什么比帮助蓝领专业人士建立更强大的企业、克服债务或为未来存钱更重要的了。

paras.en: What would you tell your younger collision self? Don’t underestimate where this industry can take you, ask more questions and save more money!
paras.zh: 你会对年轻时发生碰撞的自己说什么？不要低估这个行业可以带你去哪里，多问问题就能省更多钱！

paras.en: Nada Jokic – Business Consulting Services Manager, AkzoNobel
paras.zh: Nada Jokic – 阿克苏诺贝尔商业咨询服务经理

paras.en: How did your collision career begin? I like to say I stumbled into the industry. Shortly after college, I joined DuPont on a one-year project transitioning distributors and body shops from microfiche to PC-based paint formula retrieval. Soon after, when we began building a body shop management system, I parked myself in shops to better understand the business. That’s where I developed a real appreciation for the industry and, especially, the hardworking, down-to-earth people in it.
paras.zh: 您的碰撞生涯是如何开始的？我想说我是偶然进入这个行业的。大学毕业后不久，我加入杜邦公司，参与一个为期一年的项目，将分销商和车身修理厂从缩微胶片检索转变为基于 PC 的油漆配方检索。不久之后，当我们开始构建车身修理厂管理系统时，我把自己停在商店里，以更好地了解业务。正是在那时，我对这个行业，尤其​​是这个行业中勤奋、脚踏实地的人们产生了真正的欣赏。

paras.en: What is the proudest accomplishment of your career? Looking back, I can’t point to any one accomplishment. What has given me the most satisfaction is hearing shop owners tell me we’ve helped them grow their businesses. From DuPont’s body shop management software to AkzoNobel’s business consultants today, helping our customers succeed has always been the most rewarding part of my career.
paras.zh: 您职业生涯中最值得骄傲的成就是什么？回顾过去，我无法指出任何一项成就。让我最满意的是听到店主告诉我我们帮助他们发展了业务。从杜邦的车身修理厂管理软件到如今阿克苏诺贝尔的业务顾问，帮助我们的客户取得成功一直是我职业生涯中最有价值的部分。

paras.en: What would you tell your younger collision self? I don’t think I’d change much. If I could tell my younger self one thing, it would be to get involved with WIN sooner. Early in my career, I worked with very few women and didn’t realize how much that would change. Today, there are so many talented women leading and shaping this industry, and I’m grateful to now be part of WIN.
paras.zh: 你会对年轻时发生碰撞的自己说什么？我认为我不会改变太多。如果我能告诉年轻的自己一件事，那就是早点参与WIN。在我职业生涯的早期，我与很少的女性一起工作，并且没有意识到这会发生多大的变化。今天，有这么多才华横溢的女性领导和塑造这个行业，我很感激现在成为 WIN 的一部分。

paras.en: Kena Dacus – Owner, Dacus Auto Body & Collision Repair
paras.zh: Kena Dacus – Dacus 汽车车身和碰撞修复公司所有者

paras.en: How did your collision career begin? My path into collision repair wasn’t exactly traditional. I earned a degree in business administration from Wichita State University and began my career in accounting. In 2015, I joined my husband Chris full-time at Dacus Auto Body, just three months after he had opened. Chris brought the technical expertise, and I brought a love of numbers, business strategy and organization. Over time, I became involved in nearly every aspect of the company. What began as joining our family business grew into a genuine passion for the collision industry, its people and the opportunities we have to make it stronger.
paras.zh: 您的碰撞生涯是如何开始的？我的碰撞修复之路并不完全是传统的。我在威奇托州立大学获得了工商管理学位，并开始了我的会计职业生涯。 2015 年，我和丈夫 Chris 一起在 Dacus Auto Body 全职工作，当时距离他开业仅三个月。克里斯带来了技术专业知识，我带来了对数字、业务战略和组织的热爱。随着时间的推移，我几乎参与了公司的各个方面。从加入我们的家族企业开始，我们就对碰撞行业、该行业的员工以及我们使其变得更加强大的机会产生了真正的热情。

paras.en: What is the proudest accomplishment of your career? I’m most proud of what Chris and I have built together. We’ve grown from one collision repair location into two locations and launched Dacus Towing & Recovery, but I’m equally proud of the team and culture we’ve developed along the way. Personally, I’m also proud that my involvement has grown beyond our own businesses. Having served as president of the Kansas Auto Body Association and now on the SCRS board of directors has given me the opportunity to advocate for independent repairers and help strengthen the industry that has given our family so much.
paras.zh: 您职业生涯中最值得骄傲的成就是什么？我对克里斯和我共同创造的东西感到最自豪。我们已经从一个碰撞修复地点发展为两个地点，并推出了 Dacus Towing & Recovery，但我同样为我们一路发展的团队和文化感到自豪。就我个人而言，我也很自豪我的参与已经超出了我们自己的业务范围。曾担任堪萨斯州汽车车身协会主席，现在担任 SCRS 董事会成员，这让我有机会倡导独立维修商，并帮助加强这个为我们家庭带来巨大利益的行业。

paras.en: What would you tell your younger collision self? Take more risks. Speak up sooner, trust your instincts and don’t wait until you feel completely ready — because you may never feel completely ready. My greatest growth has come from stepping outside my comfort zone, trying something new and being willing to fail and learn as I went. I would also remind myself that I didn’t need to be an expert before I could contribute something valuable. The industry needs different perspectives, and the skills that make you different may ultimately become some of your greatest strengths.
paras.zh: 你会对年轻时发生碰撞的自己说什么？承担更多风险。早点说出来，相信你的直觉，不要等到你感觉完全准备好了——因为你可能永远不会感觉完全准备好。我最大的成长来自于走出自己的舒适区，尝试新事物，并愿意在失败中学习。我还会提醒自己，我不需要成为专家就可以贡献一些有价值的东西。这个行业需要不同的视角，而让你与众不同的技能最终可能会成为你最大的优势。

paras.en: How did your collision career begin? I grew up in my dad’s motorcycle and used car dealerships. After his bankruptcy, I worked for Mattos, a regional paint jobber in the Washington D.C. area while attending college and became fascinated with body shops. Later, while selling cars, my dealer principal asked where else I’d like to work. I said, “The body shop.” The rest is history.
paras.zh: 您的碰撞生涯是如何开始的？我在父亲的摩托车和二手车经销店长大。马托斯破产后，我在上大学期间为华盛顿特区的一名地区油漆工工作，并开始对车身修理厂着迷。后来，在销售汽车时，我的经销商负责人问我还想在哪里工作。我说：“车身修理厂。”剩下的就是历史了。

paras.en: What is the proudest accomplishment of your career? Building and selling our process-driven collision centers in 2015 was incredibly rewarding. Then came my 2.0 career—founding Consolidation Coach. What began as a part-time venture has become a leading, woman-owned M&A advisory firm in collision, allowing me to advocate for owners during one of their biggest life decisions.
paras.zh: 您职业生涯中最值得骄傲的成就是什么？ 2015 年建造和销售我们的流程驱动碰撞中心获得了令人难以置信的回报。然后是我的 2.0 职业生涯——创立整合教练。最初是一家兼职企业，后来发展成为一家领先的、由女性拥有的并购咨询公司，这让我能够在业主做出重大人生决定时为他们辩护。

paras.en: What would you tell your younger collision self? Staying power is what it takes to be successful. There will be hard times and curves in the road. Success takes vision, strength and positivity, especially when staying the course is difficult. And never let being the only woman in the room make you question whether you belong there.
paras.zh: 你会对年轻时发生碰撞的自己说什么？保持力量是成功所需要的。路上会有困难和弯路。成功需要远见、力量和积极性，尤其是在坚持到底的时候。永远不要让作为房间里唯一的女性让你怀疑自己是否属于那里。

paras.en: Shyllo Michaelis – Chief Strategy Officer, Texas Collision Centers
paras.zh: Shyllo Michaelis – 德克萨斯碰撞中心首席战略官

paras.en: How did your collision career begin? In 2010, I was recruited by Service King Founder Eddie Lennox after having been at Farmers Insurance for 15 years. I was hired to grow the Houston market as a business development manager for Service King.
paras.zh: 您的碰撞生涯是如何开始的？ 2010 年，在 Farmers Insurance 工作了 15 年之后，我被 Service King 创始人 Eddie Lennox 聘用。我受聘担任 Service King 的业务开发经理，负责拓展休斯顿市场。

paras.en: What is the proudest accomplishment of your career? By far, my greatest accomplishment is the development of people … and women in particular. Mentoring and then witnessing the growth of fellow teammates and helping them learn their full potential is so satisfying!
paras.zh: 您职业生涯中最值得骄傲的成就是什么？到目前为止，我最大的成就是人的发展……尤其是女性的发展。指导并见证队友的成长并帮助他们充分发挥潜力真是令人满足！

paras.en: What would you tell your younger collision self? I would tell my younger self to be more confident in this male-dominated space. The industry is evolving, and women now have a greater stake in the game. Women I know and love in collision repair are crushing it! I love to see it!
paras.zh: 你会对年轻时发生碰撞的自己说什么？我会告诉年轻的自己，在这个男性主导的领域要更加自信。这个行业正在不断发展，女性现在在这个游戏中拥有更大的利益。我所认识和喜爱的碰撞修复领域的女性正在粉碎它！我喜欢看它！

paras.en: Laura Kottschade – Chief Operating Officer, Jerry’s Abra Auto Body & Glass
paras.zh: Laura Kottschade – Jerry's Abra Auto Body & Glass 首席运营官

paras.en: How did your collision career begin? I was born and raised in the collision repair industry. From spending afternoons at the shop and taking tow calls while my parents plowed snow, I was always around it. The Monday after college graduation, I officially started in the parts room, learning the business from the ground up.
paras.zh: 您的碰撞生涯是如何开始的？我在碰撞修复行业出生和长大。从在商店度过一个下午，到父母犁雪时接听拖车电话，我一直都在它身边。大学毕业后的星期一，我正式开始在零件室工作，从头开始学习业务。

paras.en: What is the proudest accomplishment of your career? It’s hard to choose just one. From navigating production through COVID and unprecedented parts delays to receiving the WIN Cornerstone Award, helping grow the WIN Scholarship Program, becoming COO of our family shop and serving as WIN chair 20 years after my mom, it’s all incredibly humbling.
paras.zh: 您职业生涯中最值得骄傲的成就是什么？很难只选择一个。从应对新冠疫情和前所未有的零件延误进行生产，到获得 WIN 基石奖、帮助发展 WIN 奖学金计划、成为我们家族商店的首席运营官，以及在我母亲去世 20 年后担任 WIN 主席，这一切都令人难以置信。

paras.en: What would you tell your younger collision self? I’m only 33, so this is something I still remind myself: hold yourself to high standards, but don’t let one mistake define you. Own it, be honest, fix it, learn from it and grow. Mistakes happen; what matters is how you respond, take responsibility and move forward. I’d also tell myself that work-life balance matters. Burnout is real, and climbing out of it can be a long, difficult process. It’s okay to leave something on your desk and finish it tomorrow. Not everything has to be solved today. Taking care of yourself doesn’t mean you’re less dedicated — it allows you to show up better for your team, your customers and yourself.
paras.zh: 你会对年轻时发生碰撞的自己说什么？我才33岁，所以我仍然提醒自己：以高标准要求自己，但不要让一个错误定义你。拥有它，诚实，修复它，从中学习并成长。错误会发生；重要的是你如何回应、承担责任并继续前进。我还会告诉自己，工作与生活的平衡很重要。倦怠是真实存在的，摆脱它可能是一个漫长而艰难的过程。可以在办公桌上留下一些东西，明天再完成。并非所有事情都必须在今天解决。照顾好自己并不意味着你不那么专注——它可以让你更好地为你的团队、你的客户和你自己展示。

paras.en: Natalie Zjac – Vice President of Business Development, Crash Champions
paras.zh: Natalie Zjac – 碰撞冠军业务开发副总裁

paras.en: How did your collision career begin? My collision repair career began in 2014 when I met our founder and CEO, Matt Ebert, through a mutual friend. His passion and vision for the business were contagious, and with my background in sales and marketing, we took a chance on each other. That decision changed the course of my career and ultimately my life.
paras.zh: 您的碰撞生涯是如何开始的？我的碰撞修复职业生涯始于 2014 年，当时我通过一位共同的朋友认识了我们的创始人兼首席执行官 Matt Ebert。他对业务的热情和愿景具有感染力，而凭借我在销售和营销方面的背景，我们给了对方一个机会。这个决定改变了我的职业生涯，并最终改变了我的生活。

paras.en: What is the proudest accomplishment of your career? I always try to encourage our teams to pause and celebrate wins because we tend to move quickly from one challenge to the next. Looking back, I’m most proud of being part of the founding team that helped build one of the largest collision repair companies in the country. It’s been an incredible journey and has shaped my growth as an employee, leader and person.
paras.zh: 您职业生涯中最值得骄傲的成就是什么？我总是试图鼓励我们的团队停下来庆祝胜利，因为我们倾向于快速从一个挑战转移到下一个挑战。回顾过去，我最自豪的是成为创始团队的一员，帮助建立了美国最大的碰撞修复公司之一。这是一段令人难以置信的旅程，塑造了我作为员工、领导者和个人的成长。

paras.en: What would you tell your younger collision self? Embrace change and focus on bringing value wherever you can make the biggest impact. Stay curious, keep learning and be open to new opportunities along the way. Some of the most rewarding experiences and greatest growth will come from paths you never expected to take.
paras.zh: 你会对年轻时发生碰撞的自己说什么？拥抱变革，专注于在任何能产生最大影响的地方创造价值。保持好奇心，不断学习，并对新机会持开放态度。一些最有价值的经历和最大的成长将来自你从未想过的道路。

articles.title: BendPak Opens Third Distribution Center to Accelerate Delivery Nationwide
articles.author: Jason Stahl

paras.en: BendPak Inc. has announced the opening of its third distribution center, enabling delivery in two days or less to 92% of the U.S. population.
paras.zh: BendPak Inc. 宣布开设第三个配送中心，可在两天或更短的时间内向 92% 的美国人口配送。

paras.en: The new facility in Milford, Conn., serves New England, the Mid-Atlantic states and parts of the Great Lakes region. BendPak’s other regional hubs are in Santa Paula, Calif., serving the western half of the country, and Theodore, Ala., which now covers most of the Midwest and South. The optimized network brings next-day or two-day shipping to 40 states and Washington, D.C.
paras.zh: 位于康涅狄格州米尔福德的新设施为新英格兰、大西洋中部各州和五大湖地区的部分地区提供服务。 BendPak 的其他区域中心位于加利福尼亚州圣保拉，为该国的西半部提供服务；以及阿拉巴马州西奥多，目前覆盖了中西部和南部的大部分地区。优化后的网络可为 40 个州和华盛顿特区提供次日或两天送达服务。

paras.en: By further decentralizing inventory storage and integrating predictive stocking algorithms across all three hubs, BendPak reduces order fulfillment and shipping transit times, curbs secondary shipping emissions and minimizes the regional delays that traditionally disrupt national supply chains.
paras.zh: 通过进一步分散库存存储并在所有三个中心集成预测库存算法，BendPak 减少了订单履行和运输运输时间，抑制了二次运输排放，并最大限度地减少了传统上扰乱国家供应链的区域延误。

paras.en: “This Northeast distribution center marks a milestone in our commitment to customer-centric growth,” said Derek Burns, director of distribution center operations – East for BendPak. “In addition to scaling our footprint, we’re redefining what reliability looks like for our dealers and end-user customers. Reaching 92% of Americans in two days or less means our customers get what they need, when they need it, with unprecedented speed.”
paras.zh: BendPak 东部配送中心运营总监 Derek Burns 表示：“这个东北配送中心标志着我们致力于以客户为中心的增长的一个里程碑。” “除了扩大我们的足迹之外，我们还重新定义了经销商和最终用户客户的可靠性。在两天或更短的时间内覆盖 92% 的美国人，这意味着我们的客户可以在需要时以前所未有的速度获得他们需要的东西。”

paras.en: Over the last nine years, BendPak has expanded its product portfolio and geographic footprint. It has introduced new brands including Autostacker, JackPak, Ergochair and APEX, as well as products like OctaFlex and AP Series two-post lifts, Mobi-EVS Series EV battery lifts and Coolee portable air coolers.
paras.zh: 在过去的九年里，BendPak 扩大了其产品组合和地理覆盖范围。它推出了Autostacker、JackPak、Ergochair和APEX等新品牌，以及OctaFlex和AP系列两柱升降机、Mobi-EVS系列电动电池升降机和Coolee便携式空气冷却器等产品。

paras.en: During that time, the privately held company expanded its Santa Paula manufacturing and distribution center twice, bringing the facility to more than 400,000 square feet. It also established a new global headquarters in Agoura Hills, Calif., and increased its Alabama operations from a single distribution center in Theodore into a multi-building campus. Earlier this year, BendPak completed Phase 1 of its Donald R. Henthorn Industrial Complex in Mobile County, Ala.
paras.zh: 在此期间，这家私营公司两次扩建了圣保拉制造和分销中心，使该设施的面积超过 400,000 平方英尺。它还在加利福尼亚州阿古拉山建立了新的全球总部，并将其阿拉巴马州业务从西奥多的单一配送中心扩大到了一个多建筑园区。今年早些时候，BendPak 完成了位于阿拉巴马州莫比尔县的 Donald R. Henthorn 工业园区一期工程。

paras.en: “In today’s marketplace, business moves faster than ever, and BendPak is positioned to outpace it,” said Jeff Kritzer, president and CEO of BendPak. “Our Northeast expansion is just the latest step in our long-term plan to continuously refine our logistics network to optimize delivery times and best serve our customers.”
paras.zh: BendPak 总裁兼首席执行官 Jeff Kritzer 表示：“在当今的市场中，业务发展速度比以往任何时候都快，而 BendPak 有望超越它。” “我们的东北扩张只是我们长期计划的最新一步，我们的长期计划是不断完善我们的物流网络，以优化交货时间并最好地服务我们的客户。”

paras.en: For more information on BendPak, visit bendpak.com.
paras.zh: 有关 BendPak 的更多信息，请访问 Bendpak.com。

articles.title: Allstate’s Arity to acquire transportation intelligence, mobility analytics provider
articles.author: Teresa Moss

paras.en: The acquisition builds on Arity’s role in advancing the insurance company’s investment in data, analytics, and mobility intelligence, the release adds.
paras.zh: 新闻稿补充道，此次收购建立在 Arity 在推进保险公司对数据、分析和移动智能投资方面的作用的基础上。

paras.en: “Transportation operates as one connected system, yet the intelligence used to understand it remains fragmented across industries and data sources,” Gary Hallgren, Arity president, says in the release. “By combining Arity’s predictive insights on driving behavior and risk with INRIX’s transportation intelligence and mobility analytics, we will be uniquely positioned to deliver more robust intelligence and insights into how people, vehicles, goods, and roads interact.”
paras.zh: Arity 总裁加里·霍尔格伦 (Gary Hallgren) 在新闻稿中表示：“交通运输作为一个互联系统运行，但用于理解交通运输的情报仍然分散在各个行业和数据源中。” “通过将 Arity 对驾驶行为和风险的预测性见解与 INRIX 的交通智能和移动分析相结合，我们将处于独特的地位，能够提供关于人、车辆、货物和道路如何互动的更强大的智能和见解。”

paras.en: Bryan Mistele, INRIX cofounder and CEO, says in the release that Arity’s trillions of miles of mobility data and advanced analytics, combined with INRIX’s transportation intelligence, create an opportunity to further innovate mobility intelligence and improve transportation effectiveness and efficiency for customers across the public and private sectors.
paras.zh: INRIX 联合创始人兼首席执行官 Bryan Mistele 在新闻稿中表示，Arity 数万亿英里的移动数据和高级分析与 INRIX 的交通智能相结合，为进一步创新移动智能并为公共和私营部门的客户提高交通效率和效率创造了机会。

paras.en: Arity can expand the company’s ability to help organizations better understand how transportation works and where it is headed, according to the release.
paras.zh: 据新闻稿称，Arity 可以扩展公司的能力，帮助组织更好地了解交通运输的运作方式及其发展方向。

paras.en: The company gave examples of insurers managing risk, businesses moving goods, and public agencies improving safety and planning infrastructure.
paras.zh: 该公司列举了保险公司管理风险、企业运输货物以及公共机构改善安全和规划基础设施的例子。

paras.en: “By bringing together complementary perspectives across behavior, movement, and roads, Arity is building intelligence that can help organizations see change earlier, act with greater confidence, and create safer, more resilient communities.”
paras.zh: “通过汇集行为、运动和道路方面的互补观点，Arity 正在构建智能，帮助组织更早地看到变化，更有信心地采取行动，并创建更安全、更有弹性的社区。”

paras.en: Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton filed suit against Allstate and Arity for collecting, using, and selling data last year.
paras.zh: 德克萨斯州总检察长 Ken Paxton 去年对 Allstate 和 Arity 收集、使用和出售数据提起诉讼。

paras.en: Paxton’s suit claims the companies illegally collected and sold the data about the location and movement of Texan cell phones through “secretly embedded software in mobile apps” such as Life360. It claims Allstate and Arity paid app developers for the data and then created a database used by Allstate and other insurers.
paras.zh: Paxton 的诉讼称，这些公司通过 Life360 等“移动应用程序中秘密嵌入的软件”非法收集和出售有关德克萨斯州手机的位置和移动的数据。它声称 Allstate 和 Arity 向应用程序开发人员支付了数据费用，然后创建了 Allstate 和其他保险公司使用的数据库。

paras.en: Allstate told Repairer Driven News in a prepared statement that, “Arity IQ empowers consumers to take control of and customize their insurance pricing. Consumers do so by directing their insurer to request that Arity Services share insights about their driving data with insurers to receive pricing based on their driving behavior.”
paras.zh: Allstate 在一份准备好的声明中告诉 Repairer Driven News：“Arity IQ 使消费者能够控制和定制他们的保险定价。消费者通过指示他们的保险公司要求 Arity Services 与保险公司分享有关他们驾驶数据的见解来实现这一点，以便根据他们的驾驶行为获得定价。”

paras.en: The insurance company also said the consumers receive multiple notices that their data is being collected and used and can opt out at any time. This includes a notice at app sign-up.
paras.zh: 该保险公司还表示，消费者会收到多份通知，表明他们的数据正在被收集和使用，并且可以随时选择退出。这包括应用程序注册时的通知。

paras.en: Allstate filed a court response to Paxton’s suit in February 2025.
paras.zh: Allstate 于 2025 年 2 月对 Paxton 的诉讼提交了法庭回应。

paras.zh: 特色图片来源：Parradee Kietsirikul/iStock

articles.title: How Do EGR and Secondary Air Injection Work Together?
articles.author: Andrew Markel

paras.en: The perfect internal combustion vehicle would be able to put the exact amount of fuel and air into the combustion chamber at the exact right moment.
paras.zh: 完美的内燃车辆能够在正确的时刻将准确数量的燃料和空气注入燃烧室。

paras.en: If the perfect combustion event were to occur, you would get nothing more than water and carbon dioxide as byproduct, resulting in no unburned fuel or oxygen. Combustion would occur at the right temperature so oxides (“hyperactive” oxygen turned on by higher temperatures) would not combine with nitrogen and carbon to form nitric oxides (NOx) and carbon monoxide (CO). This perfect car would not need a catalytic converter or any other emission-control device.
paras.zh: 如果发生完美的燃烧事件，您只会得到水和二氧化碳作为副产品，从而不会产生未燃烧的燃料或氧气。燃烧会在适当的温度下发生，因此氧化物（较高温度下打开的“高活性”氧气）不会与氮和碳结合形成一氧化氮 (NOx) 和一氧化碳 (CO)。这辆完美的汽车不需要催化转换器或任何其他排放控制装置。

paras.en: What’s needed to make this happen? Direct injection into the combustion chamber is a good start. You would also need the perfect combustion chamber free from hot spots — areas of unwanted turbulence or carbon buildup.
paras.zh: 需要什么才能实现这一点？直接喷射到燃烧室是一个好的开始。您还需要完美的燃烧室，没有热点（不必要的湍流或积碳区域）。

paras.en: But, the most important ingredient you would need is an engine control computer and sensors that could measure air and fuel perfectly to calculate the best possible ignition timing and optimal combustion. This would require the super computer’s computing capacity to do millions of calculations that would constantly change due to engine speed and load.
paras.zh: 但是，您需要的最重要的组成部分是发动机控制计算机和传感器，它们可以完美地测量空气和燃料，以计算最佳的点火正时和最佳燃烧。这需要超级计算机的计算能力进行数百万次计算，这些计算会因发动机速度和负载而不断变化。

paras.en: We do not have this technology, but every year combustion chamber designs get better, engine computers get better and sensors get more sensitive.
paras.zh: 我们没有这项技术，但每年燃烧室设计都变得更好，发动机计算机变得更好，传感器变得更加灵敏。

paras.en: Currently, we have exhaust gas recirculation systems (EGR), secondary air injection and catalytic converters to reduce emissions. Let’s talk about how those work.
paras.zh: 目前，我们拥有废气再循环系统（EGR）、二次空气喷射和催化转化器来减少排放。让我们谈谈它们是如何工作的。

paras.en: EGR systems put a small amount of inert gas into the combustion chamber to control the temperatures. Since exhaust gases do not typically burn, this lowers the combustion temperature and reduces NOx emissions from the engine while allowing it to run a leaner fuel mixture.
paras.zh: EGR系统将少量惰性气体放入燃烧室以控制温度。由于废气通常不会燃烧，这会降低燃烧温度并减少发动机的氮氧化物排放，同时允许其运行更稀薄的燃料混合物。

paras.en: When things heat up in the combustion chamber to temperatures around 1,300° C or 2,500° F, oxygen and nitrogen start combining with each other and form NOx and CO.
paras.zh: 当燃烧室中的物体加热到 1,300° C 或 2,500° F 左右的温度时，氧气和氮气开始相互结合，形成氮氧化物和一氧化碳。

paras.en: By putting exhaust gases into the combustion chamber, the air/fuel mixture is watered down by the inert exhaust gases. This slows down the combustion process and lowers combustion temperatures to levels where NOx does not form.
paras.zh: 通过将废气放入燃烧室，空气/燃料混合物被惰性废气稀释。这会减慢燃烧过程并将燃烧温度降低到不会形成氮氧化物的水平。

paras.en: Unlike older EGR systems, modern EGR systems work constantly, not just during deceleration or closed-throttle conditions. Keep this in mind when trying to solve a loss of power or stumbling problem.
paras.zh: 与旧式 EGR 系统不同，现代 EGR 系统持续工作，而不仅仅是在减速或节气门关闭的情况下。在尝试解决断电或绊倒问题时请记住这一点。

paras.en: Newer vehicles with variable valve timing on both exhaust and intake camshafts can adjust timing so that a small amount of exhaust gas is sucked back into the chamber during the intake stroke.
paras.zh: 排气和进气凸轮轴上均配备可变气门正时的新型车辆可以调整正时，以便在进气冲程期间将少量废气吸回到腔室中。

paras.en: Secondary air injection systems pump outside air into the exhaust stream so unburned fuel can be burned. Early systems have a belt-driven air pump. Newer aspirated systems use the vacuum created by an exhaust pulse to pull air into the pipe. The latest systems use an electric motor to pump air. These systems are critical for the life of the catalytic converter.
paras.zh: 二次空气喷射系统将外部空气泵入排气流中，以便燃烧未燃烧的燃料。早期的系统有一个皮带驱动的气泵。较新的吸气系统利用排气脉冲产生的真空将空气吸入管道。最新的系统使用电动机来泵送空气。这些系统对于催化转化器的使用寿命至关重要。

paras.en: Electric motor systems can be found on many new vehicles like the GM LS series, Toyota V8s and California emission Ford 3.8L V6s. These systems typically are active during the first 20 to 120 seconds of engine operation by forcing air downstream into the exhaust manifolds to oxidize the hydrocarbons and carbon monoxide created by running rich at startup. This can drastically decrease the light-off time for the pre-catalysts. The system injects the correct amount of air using inputs like coolant temperature, air temperature and oxygen sensors.
paras.zh: 电动马达系统可以在许多新车上找到，例如通用汽车 LS 系列、丰田 V8 和加州排放的福特 3.8L V6。这些系统通常在发动机运行的前 20 到 120 秒内启动，迫使空气向下游进入排气歧管，氧化启动时浓油运行产生的碳氢化合物和一氧化碳。这可以大大减少预催化剂的起燃时间。该系统使用冷却剂温度、空气温度和氧气传感器等输入来注入正确数量的空气。

paras.en: The catalytic converter needs two elements provided by the EGR and air injection systems: proper temperatures to reduce NOx and oxygen to burn hydrocarbons. Under ideal conditions, a three-way catalyst can reduce somewhere between 50 and 95 percent of NOx emissions and 99.9 percent of the unburned fuel.
paras.zh: 催化转化器需要 EGR 和空气喷射系统提供的两个要素：减少氮氧化物的适当温度和燃烧碳氢化合物的氧气。在理想条件下，三效催化剂可以减少 50% 至 95% 的氮氧化物排放量以及 99.9% 的未燃烧燃料。

paras.en: It is the last stop for pollutants, and, if an emissions system upstream is compromised, it can compensate only so much before tailpipe emissions increase.
paras.zh: 它是污染物的最后一站，如果上游的排放系统受到损害，它只能在尾气排放增加之前补偿这么多。

paras.en: To properly diagnose a high-emissions vehicle, you must look at it like an engineer looking at the entire system, from the air intake to the exhaust pipe. When a vehicle is engineered, it must meet a specified emission level. To do this, an engineering team will balance the systems and make them work in harmony so the price is affordable.
paras.zh: 要正确诊断高排放车辆，您必须像工程师查看整个系统（从进气管到排气管）一样查看它。当车辆被设计时，它必须满足指定的排放水平。为此，工程团队将平衡系统并使它们协调工作，以便价格合理。

paras.en: If a vehicle has a combustion chamber design that reaches higher-than-normal temperatures, the engineers will balance out the amount of exhaust gases introduced to the combustion chamber to the size of the converter so the vehicle meets mandated emission levels and the warranty period.
paras.zh: 如果车辆的燃烧室设计达到高于正常温度，工程师将平衡引入燃烧室的废气量与转换器的尺寸，以便车辆满足规定的排放水平和保修期。

paras.en: If platinum, palladium and other precious metals were not so expensive, we would probably see larger converters and fewer emission-control devices that focus on what is happening inside the combustion chamber.
paras.zh: 如果铂、钯和其他贵金属不是那么昂贵，我们可能会看到更大的转换器和更少的排放控制装置，这些装置专注于燃烧室内发生的情况。

paras.en: If your shop is replacing a failed catalytic converter without addressing the problems upstream, you are also using a solution that is not economically viable for the consumer because they will have to replace the converter sooner.
paras.zh: 如果您的车间在没有解决上游问题的情况下更换出现故障的催化转化器，那么您使用的解决方案对于消费者来说也是不经济可行的，因为他们必须尽快更换转化器。

paras.en: What is the future? Most EGR valves are found on diesel engines and secondary air injection systems are become even more scarce on modern engines. Thanks to direct injection and better management of the air and fuel entering the engine, the need for these components is not needed.
paras.zh: 未来是什么？大多数 EGR 阀都安装在柴油发动机上，而二次空气喷射系统在现代发动机上变得更加稀缺。由于直接喷射以及对进入发动机的空气和燃油的更好管理，不需要这些组件。

articles.title: Automotive Parts Services Group CEO Jeff Koviak on Multiplying Successes
articles.author: Mary DellaValle

paras.en: This episode of DriveTime features Jeff Koviak, CEO of the Automotive Parts Services Group. In this interview, Koviak said he views industry consolidation as an inevitable evolution that can ultimately make the independent aftermarket stronger and more competitive. Rather than becoming “distracted by the noise,” he believes Automotive Parts Services Group members should remain focused on running their businesses and getting their parts through the supply chain and installed onto cars.
paras.zh: 本期 DriveTime 的主角是汽车零部件服务集团首席执行官杰夫·科维亚克 (Jeff Koviak)。在接受采访时，科维亚克表示，他认为行业整合是一种不可避免的演变，最终可以使独立售后市场变得更强大、更具竞争力。他认为，汽车零部件服务集团成员不应“被噪音分散注意力”，而应继续专注于经营自己的业务，让零部件通过供应链并安装到汽车上。

paras.en: Koviak sees consolidation creating stronger organizations through investment and greater efficiencies, helping the independent aftermarket compete more effectively with OEM service centers.
paras.zh: Koviak 认为，整合可以通过投资和提高效率创建更强大的组织，帮助独立售后市场更有效地与 OEM 服务中心竞争。

paras.en: Koviak said collaboration and shared innovation represent one of The Group’s greatest opportunities to help members grow while preserving their entrepreneurial spirit. His focus as CEO includes bringing members together through collaborative workshops where they can exchange best practices and learn from one another. While building trust takes time, Koviak added that members are increasingly recognizing the value of working together. He believes closer collaboration can multiply growth opportunities and strengthen The Group and its members.
paras.zh: Koviak 表示，协作和共享创新是集团帮助成员成长并同时保持创业精神的最佳机会之一。作为首席执行官，他的重点包括通过协作研讨会将成员聚集在一起，让他们交流最佳实践并相互学习。科维亚克补充说，虽然建立信任需要时间，但成员们越来越认识到合作的价值。他相信更紧密的合作可以增加增长机会并增强集团及其成员的实力。

paras.en: Koviak also sees data and technology as critical competitive advantages. The Group is investing in IT best-practices workshops and industry technology initiatives to identify cost-saving opportunities and share innovative approaches across its membership. Koviak said The Group’s extensive North American DIFM market data can help members optimize inventory and make smarter business decisions while supporting closer collaboration with supplier partners on supply chain needs. Ultimately, the goal is to maximize that data to improve product availability and get the right parts where they are needed.
paras.zh: Koviak 还将数据和技术视为关键的竞争优势。该集团正在投资 IT 最佳实践研讨会和行业技术计划，以确定节省成本的机会并在其成员中分享创新方法。 Koviak表示，集团广泛的北美DIFM市场数据可以帮助会员优化库存并做出更明智的业务决策，同时支持与供应商合作伙伴就供应链需求进行更密切的合作。最终的目标是最大限度地利用这些数据，以提高产品可用性并在需要的地方获得正确的零件。

paras.en: To hear more of Koviak’s insights, be sure to watch the above video.
paras.zh: 要了解 Koviak 的更多见解，请务必观看上面的视频。

paras.en: - How Koviak views consolidation as an opportunity to strengthen the independent aftermarket and its competitive position. (5:08)
paras.zh: - Koviak 如何将整合视为加强独立售后市场及其竞争地位的机会。 (5:08)

paras.en: - How greater collaboration and shared best practices can help The Group’s members grow while maintaining their entrepreneurial strengths. (7:15)
paras.zh: - 加强合作和共享最佳实践如何帮助集团成员成长，同时保持其创业优势。 （7:15）

paras.en: - How The Group is investing in data and technology to improve decision-making, inventory optimization and supply chain collaboration. (8:59)
paras.zh: - 集团如何投资数据和技术来改善决策、库存优化和供应链协作。 （8:59）

paras.en: - The value of APSG membership conferences and key takeaways of this type of collaboration. (10:56)
paras.zh: - APSG 会员会议的价值以及此类合作的要点。 （10:56）

paras.en: - Lightning Round: Koviak shares some personal insights. (13:59)
paras.zh: - 闪电回合：Koviak 分享了一些个人见解。 (13:59)

articles.title: Why There Could Be Acquisition Opportunities in Towing
articles.author: Jason Morgan

paras.en: When you think: Aftermarket acquisitions—towing likely doesn’t spring to mind. Yet the aftermarket-adjacent vehicle-hauling market could be ripe for acquisition growth opportunities, according to Rick Schwartz, co-founder and CEO of Schwartz Advisors. The investment case depends on putting trucks to work consistently. It also means developing customer relationships that support continued spending on equipment and skilled drivers.
paras.zh: 当您想到：售后市场收购——牵引时，您可能不会想到这一点。然而，Schwartz Advisors 联合创始人兼首席执行官 Rick Schwartz 表示，与售后市场相邻的车辆运输市场的收购增长机会可能已经成熟。投资案例取决于卡车的持续运行。它还意味着发展客户关系，支持设备和熟练司机的持续支出。

paras.en: Think about it: A collision can lead to several separate towing jobs. Diversifying into hauling construction and agricultural equipment could create services beyond roadside recovery. Schwartz’s assessment, shared on the latest podcast episode of SA Aftermarket Mobility Aftermarket Indicators, starts with how operators can build the capacity and customer base to serve it.
paras.zh: 想一想：一次碰撞可能会导致多次单独的牵引工作。多元化运输建筑和农业设备可以创造路边恢复以外的服务。 Schwartz 在 SA 售后移动售后市场指标的最新播客节目中分享了他的评估，首先讨论了运营商如何建立服务能力和客户群。

paras.en: The Investment Continues After the Acquisition
paras.zh: 收购后投资继续

paras.en: Building capacity carries an ongoing equipment commitment. Schwartz describes towing as a business with relatively high capital spending as a percentage of sales, a consideration for investors accustomed to companies requiring fewer owned assets. As he explained, “You have to be comfortable with the fact that you’re going to continually be buying new trucks and equipment.”
paras.zh: 能力建设需要持续的设备承诺。施瓦茨将拖车业务描述为资本支出占销售额的比例相对较高的业务，这是习惯于对自有资产要求较少的公司的投资者的考虑因素。正如他解释的那样，“你必须接受这样一个事实：你将不断购买新的卡车和设备。”

paras.en: The people operating those trucks belong in the same investment discussion. Schwartz cautioned against an acquisition strategy built around adding equipment while reducing the employees needed to use it, saying “that’s not going to work because you need to have skilled drivers driving.”
paras.zh: 操作这些卡车的人属于同一投资讨论。施瓦茨警告不要采取围绕增加设备同时减少使用设备所需员工的收购策略，他说“这是行不通的，因为你需要有熟练的司机驾驶。”

paras.en: Schwartz sees room to eliminate unnecessary expenses, while emphasizing the strategic investments required to grow. An investor pursuing additional customers or services needs to account for the trucks and skilled drivers required to fulfill that work. Utilization then helps show whether the company is putting those resources to productive use.
paras.zh: 施瓦茨认为有消除不必要开支的空间，同时强调增长所需的战略投资。寻求额外客户或服务的投资者需要考虑完成该工作所需的卡车和熟练司机。利用率有助于显示公司是否将这些资源用于生产性用途。

paras.en: That makes management’s understanding of the business particularly important. Schwartz advises investors to examine the metrics that make an individual operator successful and use those measures to guide expansion. The equipment requirements and staffing needs become part of evaluating how a company can deliver on the customer relationships it develops.
paras.zh: 这使得管理层对业务的理解尤为重要。施瓦茨建议投资者研究使个体运营商取得成功的指标，并利用这些指标来指导扩张。设备要求和人员配置需求成为评估公司如何交付其开发的客户关系的一部分。

paras.en: In towing, like many other acquisitions, the financial history needs to be understood alongside the operator’s services and customer commitments. Schwartz encourages owners to examine whether they have captured the revenue available from their work, including ancillary services for which they can legally bill. Contracts and repeat business help establish the customer relationships behind that revenue and give an owner evidence to support the company’s acquisition case.
paras.zh: 在拖车业务中，与许多其他收购一样，需要了解财务历史以及运营商的服务和客户承诺。施瓦茨鼓励业主检查他们是否从他们的工作中获得了可用的收入，包括他们可以合法计费的辅助服务。合同和重复业务有助于建立收入背后的客户关系，并为所有者提供支持公司收购案例的证据。

paras.en: The trucks’ service histories also belong in that assessment. Reviewing how the equipment has been maintained helps a buyer understand the assets it would acquire, complementing the financial records and book of business. Together, those details give the buyer a clearer picture of the operation it would be responsible for funding and managing.
paras.zh: 卡车的服务历史也属于该评估范围。审查设备的维护方式有助于买方了解其将收购的资产，补充财务记录和业务簿。总之，这些细节可以让买方更清楚地了解其负责融资和管理的业务。

paras.en: Watch the latest episode of SA Aftermarket Mobility Insights above for all of Schwartz’s acquisition insights.
paras.zh: 请观看上面最新一集的 SA 售后市场移动洞察，了解 Schwartz 的所有收购见解。

These additions provide 100% new coverage for more than 52.3 million vehicles in operation across the United States and Canada.

paras.en: The third-quarter introductions broaden WAI Global’s aftermarket portfolio across several key product categories. These include alternators, starters, wiper motors, window regulators, voltage regulators, brake calipers, solenoids, sensors and motors. The additions address coverage gaps, improve parts availability and support changing aftermarket demand.

paras.en: “Our NPI strategy remains focused on identifying meaningful coverage gaps and bringing late-model and first-to-market solutions to customers quickly,” said Ron Bernstein, president, North America, WAI Global. “Adding coverage for more than 52 million vehicles this quarter reflects the scale of that effort and helps our customers stay ahead of changing vehicle populations and replacement demand.”
paras.zh: WAI Global 北美区总裁 Ron Bernstein 表示：“我们的 NPI 战略仍然专注于识别有意义的覆盖范围差距，并快速为客户提供最新型号和率先上市的解决方案。” “本季度增加了超过 5200 万辆汽车的覆盖范围，这反映了这一努力的规模，并帮助我们的客户领先于不断变化的车辆数量和更换需求。”

articles.title: What happened when humans encountered Gigantopithecus?
articles.author: Owen Jarus

paras.en: At nearly 10 feet (3 meters) tall and around 500 pounds (230 kilograms), Gigantopithecus was the largest primate that ever lived.
paras.zh: 巨猿高近 10 英尺（3 米），重约 500 磅（230 公斤），是有史以来最大的灵长类动物。

paras.en: Foraging across the dense tropical forests of Southeast Asia between 2 million and 200,000 years ago, the giant ape may have shared the habitat with new arrivals — hominins such as Homo erectus. (Hominins are members of the group that includes modern humans, their ancestors and closely related species, after the evolutionary split from great apes.)
paras.zh: 200万至20万年前，巨猿在​​东南亚茂密的热带森林中觅食，可能与新来者——直立人等古人类——共享栖息地。 （古人类是从类人猿进化分裂后，包括现代人类、其祖先和密切相关物种的群体的成员。）

paras.en: Despite their immense size Gigantopithecus mainly consumed plants and is closely related to modern-day orangutans.
paras.zh: 尽管巨猿体型巨大，但它主要以植物为食，与现代猩猩关系密切。

paras.en: So what would have happened when Gigantopithecus encountered these human ancestors?
paras.zh: 那么当巨猿遇到这些人类祖先时会发生什么呢？

paras.en: Experts suggested a variety of possible scenarios, including that Gigantopithecus and human ancestors didn't encounter each other at all.
paras.zh: 专家提出了多种可能的情况，包括巨猿和人类祖先根本没有相遇。

paras.en: It's "very difficult to say with any certainty, as we have no direct evidence documenting interactions between Gigantopithecus and human ancestors," Renaud Joannes-Boyau, director of higher-degree research training at Southern Cross University in Australia and an archaeologist who has conducted extensive research into human evolution, told Live Science in an email.
paras.zh: 澳大利亚南十字星大学高级研究培训主任、对人类进化进行了广泛研究的考古学家雷诺·乔安妮斯·博约（Renaud Joannes-Boyau）在一封电子邮件中告诉《生活科学》，“很难肯定地说，因为我们没有直接证据记录巨猿和人类祖先之间的相互作用。”

paras.en: "That said, if we look at the broader pattern of human evolution, our lineage [Homo] has consistently behaved as an apex predator," Joannes-Boyau said. "Humans and our ancestors have shown a remarkable tendency to explore, exploit and, at times, eliminate large animals that shared their environment. I think it is reasonable to imagine that those interactions may have involved a mixture of indifference, curiosity and violence, depending on the circumstances."
paras.zh: “也就是说，如果我们从更广泛的人类进化模式来看，我们的血统（人）一直表现得像顶级掠食者，”乔安妮斯-博约说。 “人类和我们的祖先表现出了一种显着的倾向，即探索、利用，有时甚至消灭与它们共享环境的大型动物。我认为，可以合理地想象，根据具体情况，这些相互作用可能涉及冷漠、好奇和暴力的混合体。”

paras.en: Feed your curiosity with an exclusive mystery every week, solved with science and delivered direct to your inbox before it's seen anywhere else.
paras.zh: 每周都会有一个独家谜题来满足您的好奇心，这些谜题将通过科学解决，并在其他地方看到之前直接发送到您的收件箱。

paras.en: Friedemann Schrenk, a professor of paleobiology at Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz in Germany, thinks Gigantopithecus would have likely tried to avoid humans. "Humans were and are the most aggressive primates ever on earth using tools and weapons and were probably encroaching on Gigantopithecus habitats," he told Live Science in an email. Homo erectus made use of hand axes and possibly hafted spears.
paras.zh: 德国美因茨约翰内斯古腾堡大学古生物学教授弗里德曼·施伦克认为，巨猿可能会试图避开人类。他在一封电子邮件中告诉《生活科学》：“人类过去和现在都是地球上使用工具和武器的最具攻击性的灵长类动物，并且可能正在侵占巨猿的栖息地。”直立人使用手斧和可能有柄的长矛。

paras.en: Schrenk envisions the hypothetical interactions as similar to those between modern-day humans and orangutans, which has resulted in humans encroaching on orangutan habitats and the apes' populations declining. "After all, Gigantopithecus was a gigantic orangutan," he said, noting that if there was hostility in a direct encounter, early humans would have been the aggressors.
paras.zh: 施伦克设想，假设的相互作用类似于现代人类和猩猩之间的相互作用，这导致人类侵占猩猩的栖息地，导致猿类数量下降。 “毕竟，巨猿是一只巨大的猩猩，”他说，并指出，如果直接接触中存在敌意，早期人类就会成为侵略者。

paras.en: Yet it's also possible that Gigantopithecus and hominins lived in different environments in Southeast Asia, which would have minimized the number of interactions they had, said Hervé Bocherens, a professor of biogeology at the University of Tübingen in Germany.
paras.zh: 德国图宾根大学生物地质学教授 Hervé Bocherens 表示，巨猿和古人类也有可能生活在东南亚的不同环境中，这会最大限度地减少它们之间的相互作用。

paras.en: The "carbon stable isotopic ratios measured on some teeth of both taxa suggest a different habitat, closed forests for Gigantopithecus and open savannah for Homo erectus," Bocherens told Live Science in an email. However, because of limited data, "we cannot exclude that some hominins were also present in more forested environments," he added. Grinding patterns in their teeth suggest that Gigantopithecus' diet was essentially plant-based and may have included bamboo.
paras.zh: 博切伦斯在一封电子邮件中告诉《生活科学》，“在这两个类群的一些牙齿上测量的碳稳定同位素比率表明，巨猿的栖息地不同，对于直立人来说，森林是封闭的，而对于直立人来说，是开放的草原。”然而，由于数据有限，“我们不能排除一些古人类也存在于更多森林环境中，”他补充道。牙齿的磨削图案表明巨猿的饮食基本上以植物为基础，可能包括竹子。

paras.en: In a 2024 study, scientists investigated the demise of Gigantopithecus and found no evidence that hominins contributed to Gigantopithecus' extinction. Instead, they determined that the main cause was environmental change that resulted in a reduction in the forested environment where Gigantopithecus lived and foraged. In fact, hominins and Gigantopithecus may not have encountered each other at all, Yingqi Zhang, a researcher at the Chinese Academy of Sciences and first author of the paper, told Live Science in an email.
paras.zh: 在 2024 年的一项研究中，科学家对巨猿的灭绝进行了调查，没有发现任何证据表明古人类导致了巨猿的灭绝。相反，他们确定主要原因是环境变化导致巨猿生活和觅食的森林环境减少。事实上，古人类和巨猿可能根本没有相遇过，中国科学院研究员、该论文的第一作者张英奇在一封电子邮件中告诉《生活科学》。

paras.en: We can only imagine what hominins would have thought when they glimpsed these gigantic creatures. It’s not clear how hominins and Gigantopithecus would have interacted, if they ever did, said Frido Welker, a professor of biomolecular paleoanthropology at the University of Copenhagen. He thinks they would have avoided each other but they may have "been in awe when they did happen to run into each other."
paras.zh: 我们只能想象古人类看到这些巨大生物时会怎么想。哥本哈根大学生物分子古人类学教授弗里多·韦尔克 (Frido Welker) 表示，目前尚不清楚古人类和巨猿会如何相互作用，如果它们真的发生过相互作用的话。他认为他们会避开对方，但“当他们碰巧遇到对方时，他们可能会感到敬畏”。

paras.en: See how much you know about early humans with our human evolution quiz!
paras.zh: 通过我们的人类进化测验，看看您对早期人类了解多少！

paras.en: Owen Jarus is a regular contributor to Live Science who writes about archaeology and humans' past. He has also written for The Independent (UK), The Canadian Press (CP) and The Associated Press (AP), among others. Owen has a bachelor of arts degree from the University of Toronto and a journalism degree from Ryerson University.
paras.zh: 欧文·贾鲁斯 (Owen Jarus) 是《Live Science》的定期撰稿人，撰写有关考古学和人类过去的文章。他还为《独立报》（英国）、加拿大通讯社 (CP) 和美联社 (AP) 等撰稿。欧文拥有多伦多大学文学学士学位和瑞尔森大学新闻学学位。

articles.title: Cosmic 'seagull' locks eyes with the Vera C. Rubin Observatory in long-awaited test image
articles.author: Brandon Specktor

paras.en: What it is: The head of the sassy Seagull Nebula (IC 2177)
paras.zh: 它是什么：时髦的海鸥星云的头部（IC 2177）

paras.en: Where it is: Between the constellations Monoceros and Canis Major, about 3,700 light-years away
paras.zh: 它所在的位置：在麒麟座和大犬座之间，距离约 3,700 光年

paras.en: When a seagull stares you down, scientists recommend that you stare right back at it to keep your dignity (and your french fries) intact.
paras.zh: 当海鸥盯着你看时，科学家建议你也盯着它看，以保持你的尊严（和你的炸薯条）完好无损。

paras.en: Two years ago, astronomers at the Vera C. Rubin Observatory put this idea — and their brand-new telescope — to a test of cosmic proportions, aiming an experimental 144-megapixel camera at the menacing blue eye of the Seagull Nebula (IC 2177).
paras.zh: 两年前，维拉·C·鲁宾天文台的天文学家将这个想法和他们的全新望远镜用于宇宙比例测试，将实验性 144 兆像素相机瞄准海鸥星云 (IC 2177) 的险恶蓝眼。

paras.en: Located about 3,700 light-years from Earth, the Seagull Nebula is a conglomeration of three giant, billowing clouds of irradiated gas. The "head" of the bird, featured in Rubin's image above, is a cloud called Sharpless 2-292. Its pink plumage is made of hydrogen gas, which glows brightly as ionizing radiation flies forth from the young stars at the cloud's center. The bird's blue "feathers" are clouds of dust reflecting the light from young, blue stars nesting elsewhere in the region.
paras.zh: 海鸥星云距离地球约 3,700 光年，是由三个巨大的、滚滚的辐射气体云组成的聚集体。鲁宾上图所示的这只鸟的“头”是一朵名为 Sharpless 2-292 的云。它的粉红色羽毛是由氢气制成的，当电离辐射从云中心的年轻恒星飞出时，氢气会发出明亮的光。这只鸟的蓝色“羽毛”是尘埃云，反射来自该地区其他地方筑巢的年轻蓝色恒星的光线。

paras.en: It's unclear who won this stellar stare-down. If the bird appeared to blink, that's only because its eye is really the triple-star system HD 53367, a flickering trio of very young and energetic stars actively shaping the cloud around them.
paras.zh: 目前尚不清楚谁赢得了这场精彩的对视。如果这只鸟看起来眨眼，那只是因为它的眼睛实际上是三星系统 HD 53367，这是一组闪烁的非常年轻且充满活力的恒星，正在积极塑造周围的云层。

paras.en: The Rubin Observatory, meanwhile, had to avert its gaze quickly; this image is just one of about 16,000 exposures taken of the night sky between Oct. 24 and Dec. 11, 2024, according to the National Science Foundation, which co-manages Rubin along with the U.S. Department of Energy. Taken with the aforementioned Commissioning Camera (ComCam), the deep-space photos served as an early test of the observatory's hardware, software and image-processing capabilities.
paras.zh: 与此同时，鲁宾天文台不得不迅速移开目光；根据与美国能源部共同管理鲁宾的国家科学基金会的数据，这张照片只是 2024 年 10 月 24 日至 12 月 11 日期间拍摄的约 16,000 张夜空照片中的一张。这些深空照片是使用上述调试相机（ComCam）拍摄的，是对天文台硬件、软件和图像处理能力的早期测试。

paras.en: ComCam's test image is remarkably crisp — but what's even more impressive is that Rubin has since upgraded to a camera with more than 20 times the field of view. The Legacy Survey of Space and Time Camera currently mounted on the observatory's Simonyi Survey Telescope takes 3,200-megapixel images of the night sky every 30 seconds, completing a full scan of the entire southern sky every few nights, Tony Tyson, Rubin's chief scientist, previously told Live Science.
paras.zh: ComCam 的测试图像非常清晰，但更令人印象深刻的是 Rubin 此后升级到了视野超过 20 倍的相机。鲁宾首席科学家托尼·泰森此前告诉《Live Science》，目前安装在天文台西蒙尼巡天望远镜上的传统时空巡天相机每 30 秒拍摄 3,200 兆像素的夜空图像，每隔几个晚上完成对整个南部天空的全面扫描。

paras.en: Now that the Legacy Survey of Space and Time has officially begun, Rubin will spend the next 10 years photographing the sky night after night, creating a time-lapse movie of the universe that is expected to reveal millions of cosmic wonders, from exploding supernovas to newfound comets and exoplanets. Perhaps it will even spot another bird.
paras.zh: 现在，时空遗产调查已经正式开始，鲁宾将在接下来的十年里夜复一夜地拍摄天空，制作一部宇宙延时电影，预计将揭示数以百万计的宇宙奇观，从爆炸的超新星到新发现的彗星和系外行星。也许它甚至会发现另一只鸟。

paras.en: Get the world’s most fascinating discoveries delivered straight to your inbox.
paras.zh: 将世界上最迷人的发现直接发送到您的收件箱。

paras.en: Like what you see? Take a look at the hidden details in the Vera C. Rubin Observatory's debut images here.
paras.zh: 喜欢你所看到的吗？在这里查看维拉·C·鲁宾天文台首张图像中隐藏的细节。

paras.en: Brandon is the space / physics editor at Live Science. With more than 20 years of editorial experience, his writing has appeared in The Washington Post, Reader's Digest, CBS.com, the Richard Dawkins Foundation website and other outlets. He holds a bachelor's degree in creative writing from the University of Arizona, with minors in journalism and media arts. His interests include black holes, asteroids and comets, and the search for extraterrestrial life.
paras.zh: 布兰登是《Live Science》的空间/物理编辑。凭借 20 多年的编辑经验，他的文章曾发表在《华盛顿邮报》、《读者文摘》、CBS.com、理查德·道金斯基金会网站和其他媒体上。他拥有亚利桑那大学创意写作学士学位，辅修新闻学和媒体艺术。他的兴趣包括黑洞、小行星和彗星，以及寻找外星生命。

articles.title: How purported tales of consuming vampire blood and organs spread in the 18th century
articles.author: John Blair

paras.en: In the 17th and 18th centuries, the fear of vampires reached extraordinarily heights. People believed corpses could reanimate and wander around, terrorizing villages and spreading disease. They went to extreme lengths to prevent a vampire from rising. Some chopped the deceased person's head off, others placed sickles across their necks. Many were placed face down in their graves. In one grave in Poland, the remains of a boy were found with an iron padlock around his foot.
paras.zh: 在 17 世纪和 18 世纪，人们对吸血鬼的恐惧达到了非同寻常的高度。人们相信尸体可以复活并四处游荡，恐吓村庄并传播疾病。他们竭尽全力阻止吸血鬼的崛起。一些人砍下了死者的头，另一些人将镰刀架在死者的脖子上。许多人被面朝下埋在坟墓里。在波兰的一个坟墓中，发现了一具男孩的遗骸，他的脚上锁着一把铁挂锁。

paras.en: In this excerpt from "Killing the Dead: Vampire Epidemics from Mesopotamia to the New World" (Princeton University Press, 2025), author and historian John Blair reveals the impact the printed press had on the spread of vampiric lore — and the grizzly purported practice of ingesting the blood and organs of a vampire to prevent other people becoming one.
paras.zh: 在《杀死死者：从美索不达米亚到新世界的吸血鬼流行病》（普林斯顿大学出版社，2025 年）的摘录中，作家兼历史学家约翰·布莱尔揭​​示了印刷媒体对吸血鬼传说传播的影响，以及据称摄入吸血鬼的血液和器官以防止其他人成为吸血鬼的做法。

paras.en: With the invention of printing, the circulation of European stories about restless corpses moved up several gears. Occasional early references were followed by a clutch of theological and philosophical discussions during c. 1580-1610, and then — from the 1670s — a steadily growing volume of printed academic and historical debate and commentary, reaching a climax in 1732.
paras.zh: 随着印刷术的发明，欧洲有关不安尸体的故事的传播速度加快了几个档次。偶尔的早期参考文献之后会出现一些神学和哲学讨论。 1580-1610 年，然后从 1670 年代开始，学术和历史辩论和评论的印刷量稳步增长，并在 1732 年达到顶峰。

paras.en: Another landmark came in 1746 when the Benedictine scholar Dom Augustin Calmet published his survey of supernatural beings, which was quickly reissued in several editions, including an English one of 1759. This book's section on vampires was the most influential academic work on the subject ever published. Its straightforwardly evidence-based approach was a breath of fresh air after a long series of increasingly derivative works.
paras.zh: 另一个里程碑出现在 1746 年，当时本笃会学者多姆·奥古斯丁·卡尔梅特 (Dom Augustin Calmet) 发表了他对超自然生物的调查，该调查很快就以多个版本重新出版，其中包括 1759 年的英文版本。这本书中有关吸血鬼的部分是迄今为止出版的有关该主题的最有影响力的学术著作。在一系列日益衍生的作品之后，其直接的基于证据的方法为人们带来了一股新鲜空气。

paras.en: It achieved its remarkable popularity because it entered the market at the right point: saturated with so much fragmented and repetitive discussion of "vampires" (still a relatively new word), the reading public wanted a textbook. Calmet inspired a huge progeny of followers and popularisers, bringing the stories to a much wider readership; a good example of the genre is the Histoire des vampires et des spectres malfaisants [History of Vampires and Malevolent Specters] of 1820, a pocketbook that re-packages Calmet for the mass market.
paras.zh: 它之所以如此受欢迎，是因为它进入市场的时机恰到好处：充斥着对“吸血鬼”（仍然是一个相对较新的词）的如此多零碎和重复的讨论，读者想要一本教科书。卡尔梅特启发了大批追随者和普及者，将这些故事带给了更广泛的读者。该类型的一个很好的例子是 1820 年的 Histoire des vampires et des specters malfaisants [吸血鬼和恶毒幽灵的历史]，这是一本针对大众市场重新包装 Calmet 的小册子。

paras.en: Calmet's book remains the ultimate source of much modern vampire literature in Europe and America, both fictional and supposedly historical, and was transformative in bringing the topic to a wider reading public. There and elsewhere, stories were now frozen on the printed page, where later generations could read them. But they were stories still: not necessarily more reliable, and by no means stable in transmission.
paras.zh: 卡尔梅特的书仍然是欧洲和美国许多现代吸血鬼文学的最终来源，无论是虚构的还是历史上的，并且在将这个主题带给更广泛的读者群体方面具有变革性。在那里和其他地方，故事现在被冻结在印刷版上，供后人阅读。但它们仍然是故事：不一定更可靠，而且传播也绝不稳定。

paras.en: The complexity of interactions between learned discourse and popular practice is illustrated by one particularly bizarre and repellant (not to say dangerous) strand in the belief-system. This is the practice of ingesting blood or organs from a supposed vampire corpse, or ashes derived from burning them, as a remedy for vampire-induced illness.
paras.zh: 信仰体系中的一个特别奇怪和令人厌恶（更不用说危险）的部分说明了学术话语和流行实践之间相互作用的复杂性。这是一种从所谓的吸血鬼尸体中摄取血液或器官，或燃烧它们所得的灰烬的做法，作为治疗吸血鬼引起的疾病的方法。

paras.en: Although not wholly dissimilar from the idea that victims will recover as they watch the smoke rise from burning vampire organs — already known in 11th-century England — its shocking physicality sets it apart. Did people in pre-modern Europe really do this?
paras.zh: 尽管这与受害者在看到吸血鬼器官燃烧而升起的烟雾时会康复的想法并不完全不同（这在 11 世纪的英国就已为人所知），但其令人震惊的物理特性使其与众不同。前现代欧洲的人们真的这样做过吗？

paras.en: A complicating factor is the medicinal use of human blood and bodyparts, in accordance with the theories of the physician, philosopher, and alchemist "Paracelsus" (Theophrastus von Hohenheim, c. 1493–1541). A brilliant experimenter, Paracelsus believed that substances healed through occult 'influences' or 'spirits,' the most powerful being those derived from what they were meant to cure: the human body.
paras.zh: 根据医生、哲学家和炼金术士“Paracelsus”（Theophrastus von Hohenheim，c. 1493–1541）的理论，一个复杂的因素是人类血液和身体部位的药用用途。帕拉塞尔苏斯是一位杰出的实验家，他相信物质可以通过神秘的“影响”或“精神”来治愈，其中最强大的是那些源自它们要治愈的东西：人体。

paras.en: The fact that medicine now rejects these hypotheses should not make us view them patronizingly: in the early modern period, ingesting or anointing with substances from Egyptian mummies or the blood of executed criminals seemed as rational as doing the same with any other substance. These Paracelsian ideas entered popular practice: at a beheading in Vienna in 1668/9, a man ran forward and caught the spouting blood to cure his epilepsy.
paras.zh: 医学现在拒绝这些假设的事实不应让我们以居高临下的态度看待它们：在现代早期，摄入或涂抹来自埃及木乃伊或被处决的罪犯的血液的物质似乎与使用任何其他物质一样合理。这些帕拉塞尔西式的想法进入了大众实践：1668/9 年在维也纳发生的一次斩首事件中，一名男子跑上前去，抓住了喷出的鲜血，以治疗他的癫痫症。

paras.en: The tangled story of consuming blood from vampire corpses starts in a different and very unexpected place. In 1687, a major ethnographical account of parts of West Africa by the Capuchin missionary Giovanni Antonio Cavazzi was published in Bologna. In it, Cavazzi describes magical and medical practices among the Mbundu of Angola, including a method of obtaining vital curative fluid from undecayed corpses:
paras.zh: 消耗吸血鬼尸体血液的错综复杂的故事始于一个不同且非常出乎意料的地方。 1687 年，嘉布遣会传教士乔瓦尼·安东尼奥·卡瓦齐 (Giovanni Antonio Cavazzi) 在博洛尼亚出版了一部关于西非部分地区的重要民族志记录。卡瓦齐在书中描述了安哥拉姆本杜人的魔法和医疗实践，包括从未腐烂的尸体中获取重要的治疗液体的方法：

paras.en: When they are in a fresh and intact state when unearthed, their heads are cut from their bodies, from which it is said that blood flows out (which may happen through some illusion or deceit). It is collected and made into poultices for the sick, or mixed into their food, which infallibly guarantees health. Thereafter the dead person, having lost his strength, will no longer be able to harass them.
paras.zh: 当它们出土时处于新鲜且完整的状态时，它们的头被从身体上切下来，据说血液会从中流出（这可能是通过某种幻觉或欺骗而发生的）。人们将其收集起来制成膏剂给病人使用，或者混入食物中，这无疑保证了健康。此后，死者失去了力量，将无法再骚扰他们。

paras.en: From Angola to Paris: in May 1693, a story appeared in the society magazine Mercure Galant. The author was the courtier and polymath Pierre des Noyers (1607–93), who spent several years in Poland in the entourage of Queen Louise-Marie. Much earlier, in 1639, he had written to a friend about the being known as upior (Ruthenian) or striga (Polish): born with teeth; eating its shroud and then its hands and arms in the coffin; causing successive deaths of family members; and extinguished by decapitation and release of pent-up blood.
paras.zh: 从安哥拉到巴黎：1693 年 5 月，社会杂志《Mercure Galant》上刊登了一个故事。作者是朝臣兼博学者皮埃尔·德·诺瓦耶（Pierre des Noyers，1607-93 年），他在路易丝·玛丽王后的随从身边度过了几年。更早的时候，即 1639 年，他曾写信给一位朋友，谈到了被称为 upior（鲁塞尼亚语）或 striga（波兰语）的情况：生来就有牙齿；吃掉它的裹尸布，然后吃掉它在棺材里的手和手臂；造成家庭成员连续死亡；并通过斩首和释放被压抑的血液而熄灭。

paras.en: This story is rather highly coloured (eating the hands and arms is unusual), but it does probably originate in genuine oral accounts of the shroud-chewer belief.
paras.zh: 这个故事相当有色彩（吃手和手臂是不寻常的），但它确实可能起源于咀嚼裹尸布信仰的真实口头记录。

paras.en: Very different is des Noyers’s account from 1693. Now the striges and upierz have become corpse-hijacking demons: 'It is said that the demon takes this blood from the body of a living person, or from certain animals, and carries it into a dead body; for it is alleged that the demon goes out from this corpse during a certain period, between noon and midnight, after which it returns and stores there the blood that it has gathered.'
paras.zh: 德·诺瓦耶斯 1693 年的叙述截然不同。现在，斯特里奇斯和乌皮尔兹已经成为劫持尸体的恶魔：“据说，恶魔从活人或某些动物的身体中获取血液，并将其带入死者的身体；”因为据称恶魔会在中午和午夜之间的某个时间段内从这具尸体中出来，之后它会返回并在那里储存它所收集的血液。

paras.en: The blood comes out of the mouth, nose, and ears of the corpse, the corpse swims in blood, and it starts to eat its shroud. The demon especially troubles former associates and relatives of the dead 'host,' appearing to them in the guise of parents or friends, and does not leave until all the family members have died in succession. The remedy is to exhume the corpse, which is found soft, flexible, bloated, and red:
paras.zh: 鲜血从尸体的嘴、鼻子、耳朵里流出来，尸体在血中游动，开始吃它的裹尸布。该恶魔特别困扰死去“宿主”的前同事和亲属，以父母或朋友的名义出现在他们面前，直到所有家庭成员相继死亡后才离开。补救措施是挖出尸体，发现尸体柔软、有弹性、肿胀、呈红色：

paras.en: When they are found in that state, having the likeness of those who had appeared in dreams, their heads are cut off and their hearts are opened, and a quantity of blood flows out. It is collected and kneaded into flour, which is made into bread, which is a certain remedy to guarantee against such a terrible affliction. After the heads [of the dead people] have been cut off, those whom the Spirit torments at night are no longer troubled by it, and are well thereafter.
paras.zh: 当他们被发现处于那种状态，具有梦中出现的样子时，他们的头被砍掉，他们的心被打开，大量的血液流出。人们把它收集起来，揉成面粉，制成面包，这是一种可以防止这种可怕痛苦的药物。当[死人]的头被砍下来之后，那些在夜间受圣灵折磨的人就不再受其困扰，从此以后就安然无恙了。

paras.en: This narrative has problems. The idea of the demon using the corpse as a safe-deposit for its hoard of blood seems to be unique; so, probably, is the time-slot between noon and midnight. These read like clerical rationalizations, perhaps fed to des Noyers by some Polish priest and overlaid on his earlier, more authentic observations. But more fundamentally, it seems obvious that des Noyers’s account of Poland shamelessly re-works Cavazzi's account of Angola, published eight years previously.
paras.zh: 这个叙述有问题。恶魔利用尸体作为其宝藏血液的保险箱的想法似乎是独一无二的。中午和午夜之间的时间段可能也是如此。这些读起来像是教士的合理化解释，可能是由一些波兰牧师提供给德诺耶斯的，并覆盖在他早期更真实的观察之上。但更根本的是，很明显，德诺耶斯对波兰的描述无耻地重写了卡瓦齐八年前发表的对安哥拉的描述。

paras.en: It might not be quite so simple. An earlier common source, still unidentified, remains possible. The descriptions of mixing blood into food and poultices look remarkably close to Paracelsian ideas, extended from ordinary corpses to undead ones: was even Cavazzi's account distorted by his own medical learning? But in any case des Noyers’s account is a piece of unprincipled plagiarism, worthless as evidence for Polish folk-belief.
paras.zh: 事情可能没那么简单。更早的共同来源（尚未确定）仍然是可能的。将血液混合到食物和药膏中的描述看起来非常接近帕拉塞尔的想法，从普通尸体延伸到不死尸体：甚至卡瓦齐的描述也被他自己的医学知识所扭曲吗？但无论如何，德诺耶斯的叙述都是无原则的抄袭，作为波兰民间信仰的证据毫无价值。

paras.en: Even so, it has bounced down through the echo-chambers of vampire literature ever since. The following year, a lawyer called Marigner built on the narrative — which he took at face value — with long philosophical musings on the nature of vampires. Inevitably, in 1746, it was republished in Calmet's book, which made it permanently available to vampire-aware readers.
paras.zh: 即便如此，从那时起，它就在吸血鬼文学的回声室中回响。第二年，一位名叫马里格纳的律师在这个叙述的基础上——他只相信表面价值——对吸血鬼的本质进行了长期的哲学思考。 1746 年，它不可避免地在卡尔梅特的书中重新出版，这使得了解吸血鬼的读者可以永久阅读它。

paras.en: While otherwise faithful to des Noyers, Calmet's version irons out the motif of demonic corpse-possession by calling this predator a vampire 'or a demon in its form.' This process of moulding to a more familiar template culminates in a recent version that presents the story as straightforward ethnographic reporting, omitting the demonic motif completely.
paras.zh: 虽然卡尔梅特的版本在其他方面忠于德诺耶斯，但通过称这个掠食者为吸血鬼“或其形式的恶魔”，消除了恶魔占有尸体的主题。这种塑造更熟悉的模板的过程在最近的版本中达到了顶峰，该版本将故事呈现为简单的民族志报告，完全省略了恶魔主题。

paras.en: - 'It gives us a glimpse of a different kind of Viking life': Archaeologist Neil Price on the sea-kings, sorcerers and Sámi who lived during the Viking Age
paras.zh: - “它让我们一睹不同的维京生活”：考古学家尼尔·普莱斯谈维京时代的海王、巫师和萨米人

paras.en: - 'News reports tweaked the science to speak to contemporary anxieties': How Neanderthal extinction is a projection of our own, modern fears
paras.zh: -“新闻报道调整了科学以应对当代的焦虑”：尼安德特人的灭绝如何是我们现代恐惧的投射

paras.en: - 'His urine goes on tour around Europe, showing the kings and queens this glowing pee': The weird world of alchemy before chemistry
paras.zh: -“他的尿液在欧洲巡回演出，向国王和王后展示了这种发光的尿液”：化学之前的炼金术的奇怪世界

paras.en: So far, this has just been a morality tale of plagiarism and uncritical copying. But in 1713, at Dąbrówka (now western Ukraine), some villagers were tried in the Uniate episcopal court for exhuming a woman's corpse and mutilating it in inventive ways. They admitted to the exhumation (because the dead woman had been walking around and attacking people), and to drinking the corpse's blood mixed with vodka. They denied cutting out the heart, mixing the blood into flour, and baking cakes with it, but the judges were sceptical and made them swear an oath.
paras.zh: 到目前为止，这只是一个剽窃和不加批判的复制的道德故事。但 1713 年，在达布罗夫卡（Dąbrówka）（现乌克兰西部），一些村民因挖掘出一名妇女的尸体并以创造性的方式肢解而在东联主教法庭受到审判。他们承认挖掘尸体（因为死者曾四处走动并攻击人），并承认喝了与伏特加混合的尸体血。他们否认切出心脏，将血与面粉混合，并用它烤蛋糕，但法官对此表示怀疑，并让他们发誓。

paras.en: This will sound very familiar to readers of early modern witch trials, where suspects were regularly bullied into admitting bizarre fantasies formulated by the persecutors. In this case, it seems clear that at least the idea of the blood-cakes was suggested by the judges; the same could be true of the blood-drinking, even though the accused were induced to confess that. It is distinctly possible, not to say likely, that an ordinary corpse-killing was embellished with luridly fictitious detail by judges who knew des Noyers's report from twenty years earlier.
paras.zh: 对于现代早期女巫审判的读者来说，这听起来非常熟悉，嫌疑人经常被迫承认迫害者提出的奇异幻想。在这种情况下，很明显，至少血饼的想法是由法官提出的。即使被告是被诱使承认这一点的，吸血的情况也可能如此。显然有可能，而不是说有可能，一场普通的尸体屠杀被二十年前了解德诺瓦报告的法官用耸人听闻的虚构细节修饰。

paras.en: Help us improve Live Science Pro: We're always trying to make our content better. Leave us feedback about Pro here.
paras.zh: 帮助我们改进 Live Science Pro：我们一直在努力让我们的内容变得更好。请在此处给我们留下有关 Pro 的反馈。

paras.en: Killing the Dead provides the first in-depth, global account of one of the world’s most widespread yet misunderstood forms of mass hysteria—the vampire epidemic. In a spellbinding narrative, John Blair takes readers from ancient Mesopotamia to present-day Haiti to explore a macabre frontier of life and death where corpses are believed to wander or do harm from the grave, and where the vampire is a physical expression of society’s inexplicable terrors and anxieties.
paras.zh: 《杀戮死者》首次在全球范围内对吸血鬼流行病进行了深入的描述，这是世界上最普遍但又被误解的大规模歇斯底里症之一。在引人入胜的叙述中，约翰·布莱尔带领读者从古代美索不达米亚到当今的海地，探索生与死的可怕边界，那里的尸体被认为在坟墓中徘徊或造成伤害，而吸血鬼则是社会无法解释的恐惧和焦虑的具体表现。

paras.en: John Blair is an emeritus fellow of The Queen’s College, Oxford, and emeritus professor of medieval history and archaeology at the University of Oxford. His many books include "Building Anglo-Saxon England" (Princeton University Press), "The Church in Anglo-Saxon Society, and The Anglo-Saxon Age: A Very Short Introduction" (Oxford University Press).
paras.zh: 约翰·布莱尔是牛津大学女王学院的名誉研究员，也是牛津大学中世纪历史和考古学的名誉教授。他的许多著作包括《建设盎格鲁撒克逊英格兰》（普林斯顿大学出版社）、《盎格鲁撒克逊社会中的教会和盎格鲁撒克逊时代：非常简短的介绍》（牛津大学出版社）。
